correctness.rationale: The graph K1 join C5 has precisely six singleton balls, five four-point rim neighborhoods and one full ball. For each output v the maximal average can be linearized by choosing one eligible averaging row. Counting gives 2*3^5=486 centered matrices and 7*5^5=21,875 uncentered. Independent construction and exhaustive integer Bareiss positive-definiteness tests on 216I-(12A)^T(12A) and 5832I-25(12A)^T(12A) found exactly one and five exceptions, respectively, with no floating-point tolerance. The exceptional centered winner has norm^2=3/2 with simple positive eigenvector (5,1^5). The five rotated uncentered winners have simple positive Perron eigenvectors (1,1,y,z,z,y) with lambda solving 64lambda^3-120lambda^2+27lambda-1=0 in (1.62,1.621). Strict ball-selection inequalities establish that these linear candidates attain the nonlinear operator and exhaust extremizers, up to signs and rotations. The exact finite enumeration is exhaustive, not an extrapolation or an opaque output log.
